quran.note: True to his promise, a messenger and a prophet who enjoined prayer and zakah on his people.
Ibrahim and Ismail raise the foundations of the House and pray for a messenger from among their descendants.
Ibrahim settles some of his descendants in an uncultivated valley near the Sacred House.
The forbearing boy and the dream; the boy is ransomed with a great sacrifice. The Qur’an does not name him here.
Ismail, Idris and Dhul-Kifl, all of the patient.
Ismail, Elisha and Dhul-Kifl are among the outstanding.
Ya’qub’s sons say they will worship the God of Ibrahim, Ismail and Ishaq.

hadith.narrator: Ibn Abbas, through Sa’id ibn Jubayr
hadith.summary: In the long report of Hajar and Ismail, Ismail grew up among the Jurhum tribe who settled near Zamzam, learned their Arabic and married a woman from among them. His father Ibrahim visited twice while he was away and then met him near Zamzam, sharpening arrows; they raised the foundations of the Ka’ba together and prayed that Allah accept their work. The report does not mention a sacrifice.
The Prophet ﷺ said Allah chose Kinana from the descendants of Ismail, Quraysh from Kinana, Banu Hashim from Quraysh, and himself from Banu Hashim.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: Concludes that the son Ibrahim was told to sacrifice was Ismail. Names Ibn Abbas (reported through Sa’id ibn Jubayr, al-Sha’bi, Yusuf ibn Mihran, Mujahid and Ata’), Ibn Umar, al-Sha’bi (who said he saw the ram’s horns in the Ka’ba), al-Hasan al-Basri, Muhammad ibn Ka’b al-Qurazi, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and Imam Ahmad as holding it. He also cites a report from Safiyya bint Shayba, through Uthman ibn Talha, that the Prophet ﷺ saw the ram’s horns in the Ka’ba. The abridged text gives no grade for that report and we have not checked it.

differences.question: Which son was Ibrahim told to sacrifice (37:102)?

views.who: Ibn Abbas, Ibn Umar, Mujahid, al-Sha’bi, al-Hasan al-Basri, Imam Ahmad and others listed by Ibn Kathir
views.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com), on 37:102
views.view: Ismail. Ibn Kathir holds this view and treats Ishaq as a mistaken identification.

views.who: The Jewish text, as Ibn Kathir describes it
views.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com), on 37:102; the Bible text (Genesis 22:1-14, NRSVUE) read on BibleGateway
views.view: The Bible names the son as Isaac (Genesis 22:2, read by us on BibleGateway). Ibn Kathir argues that the name was inserted into the Jewish text.

differences.note: The Qur’an does not name the son (37:99-107). The good news of Ishaq is given afterwards (37:112).
